text:
Remote team handoffs always force a difficult choice between convenience and control. When you prioritize convenience, you lean into asynchronous workflows and lightweight documentation, which keeps momentum high and prevents bottlenecks. However, you inevitably lose some granular oversight.

When you prioritize control, you implement rigorous sync meetings and strict verification steps. This reduces error rates but often introduces friction that slows the entire engine down. The best remote leaders don't pick one; they decide which tasks require high-fidelity handoffs and which can thrive on pure autonomy.
